claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed primarily by the thermodynamic free-energy landscape predicted by CALPHAD.
A critical free-energy difference between BCC and a more stable low-temperature phase triggers transformation.
The lower-temperature product may be FCC or an intermetallic phase.
Changing the cooling rate will alter the phase transformation behavior.
Nucleation and growth of an emerging FCC or intermetallic phase occur when the free-energy difference surpasses a critical threshold.
Nucleation and growth of the emerging phase mediate dissolution of the BCC phase.
On cooling, the free energy of BCC increases relative to that of an alternative phase.
Once the free-energy difference exceeds a threshold, the thermodynamic driving force overcomes kinetic barriers and produces phase transformation.
The BCC-to-alternative-phase transformation temperature will correlate with the free-energy difference predicted by CALPHAD.
Slower cooling rates will produce a more complete transformation toward the thermodynamically predicted phases.
A sample maintained at high temperature, or cooled at a rate predicted to preserve BCC, will show no transformation during processing.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply only within composition and temperature ranges in which CALPHAD predictions for Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 are validated.
Outside those ranges, kinetic effects may dominate or alternative phases may form.
Diffusion limitations may shift observed transformation temperatures and rates.
